new.n: The money belt under the oak, Walker Tavern, Cambridge Junction
new.pl: Walker Tavern yard at Cambridge Junction (US-12 / M-50), Lenawee Co; Cambridge Junction Historic State Park. Pin at GNIS Cambridge Junction, not adjusted to the building
new.v: A murdered traveller's money belt of gold (tradition; no amount)
new.st: The WPA guide to Michigan (1941) tells that a gold-carrying speculator or cattleman was murdered in the tavern's 'murder room' and robbed of his money belt. Some months later the ground under one of the giant oaks in the inn yard showed traces of digging, presumably where the belt had been buried. Nine Potawatomi graves are said to lie under the big oak. Pin is the tavern crossroads, not a spot.
new.t: Legend from a 1941 guidebook; no period telling yet. State historic site with graves under the oak: no digging, look only.
new.warn: State historic site and graves: look only.
src: Michigan: A Guide to the Wolverine State (WPA, 1941), Tour 1, about p. 392
pinev: GNIS Cambridge Junction (42.0589,-84.2211), the US-12 / M-50 crossroads where the tavern stands; building not fixed on imagery, ring 150 m.
new.tovw: Lead grade D (treasure thread): 1941 WPA guide only

set.pl: Kelly's Bluff, Dubuque: Kelly's property 'directly behind St Raphael's Cathedral, S end of Cardiff St, edge of the bluff' (WPA Iowa guide 1938); ring also covers a round bluff-top structure
pinev: WPA Iowa guide (1938): directly behind St Raphael's Cathedral, S end of Cardiff St, at the bluff edge (GNIS Kellys Bluff 42.4958,-90.6687).

A round structure about 40 m across at 42.4944,-90.6726 (1930 Iowa ortho, 2020 lidar) was a candidate for the 1914 reservoir dig, but the 1909 and 1950 Sanborns show no reservoir there: unconfirmed. Pin midway, 400 m ring covers both.

src: Iowa: A Guide to the Hawkeye State (WPA, 1938), Dubuque
Sanborn maps, Dubuque, 1909 sheet 61; 1950 sheets 47, 61 (PC (b) read): no reservoir at the round structure
